title: Backpressure amplification from sticky auth lease retries caused regional 429 wave
creator: Marcus Patel
description: Summary: On 2025-02-14 a regional 429 storm lasted ~42 minutes for a subset of production tokens. Traffic analysis showed a dramatic amplification where aggressive retry loops from edge auth clients (gateway edge agents) caused concentrated load on the central lease/token service and the quota enforcer. Sticky lease retries (clients re-requesting short-lived auth leases without exponential backoff/jitter) caused a feedback loop: auth service latency increased -> gateway retries synchronously -> quota enforcer perceived many simultaneous token bursts and applied hard quotas resulting in regional starvation. Impact: some customers experienced elevated 429s and request tail latency; headroom for Dedicated pools in the affected region dropped 60% for 20 minutes. This ticket captures the postmortem, mitigations applied, and the action plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-14T09:12Z - First pager alert: gateway 429 rate > 5x baseline in us-west-2
2025-02-14T09:15Z - Triage: partial mitigation toggled (increase short-term token allowance) to reduce immediate 429s
2025-02-14T09:22Z - Observed auth lease call latency climb from 30ms -> 350ms correlated to retry bursts
2025-02-14T09:28Z - Rolled out emergency throttle policy at edge to introduce a soft circuit-breaker (10min window)
2025-02-14T09:44Z - 429 rates subsided to near-baseline after edge throttling and additional queuing
root_cause: A combination of (1) edge clients implementing immediate/linear retries for failed auth lease requests with very short retry intervals, and (2) the quota enforcer treating temporary auth lease storms as sustained token consumption without differentiating short spike vs sustained demand. The auth lease cache had a correctness window where leases were considered missing for ~200ms after renewal, causing duplicate lease requests (sticky reads). Together these amplified into a self-reinforcing backpressure loop that pushed the quota enforcer into hard limits for some regional pools.
mitigation_taken: Emergency: enabled edge soft-throttles and increased short-term quota windows to allow in-flight requests to drain (rollout 09:28 UTC)
Hotfix: patched gateway agent to add a randomized retry jitter and cap rapid retry burst (deployed 09:40 UTC)
Monitoring: created immediate Grafana alert for auth-lease-latency > 200ms AND 5xx-retry-rate > 2%
Customer comms: CS notified affected accounts with ETA and workaround guidance
action_items: Ivy Chen: Implement a local lease cache validation boundary (200ms-write-through) to eliminate duplicate renewals; review and land by 2025-02-21; estimate 3 points; status: In Progress

Marcus Patel: Add exponential backoff + random jitter library into gateway SDK and enforce default retries for auth lease calls; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4621 ; due 2025-02-18; status: In Review

Diane Rosario (SRE): Add a quota-enforcer metric distinguishing 'spike' vs 'sustained' consumption and update enforcement policy to include short spike forgiveness window; due 2025-03-03; status: Open

SRE/QA: Create chaos test that simulates auth lease flapping and ensures the system maintains <5% 429 amplification; test harness and runbook in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/gateway/lease-chaos ; due 2025-03-07; status: Open

Product: Update runbook and on-call playbook with clear step-by-step for edge soft-throttles, including runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/gateway-429-playbook ; owner: Priya Nair; due 2025-02-25; status: Open

Observability: Build dashboard tile 'Lease Retry Amplification' and a per-region 'effective-headroom' gauge; dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/leases/amplification ; owner: Omar Singh; due 2025-02-24; status: In Progress
Engineering: Add end-to-end test for quota-enforcer release that validates quota attribution under short spike patterns; owner: ENG-QE team; due 2025-03-10; status: Open
postmortem_notes: Decision: Prefer client-side throttling and local circuit-breaking over aggressive central throttles for short-lived auth issues
Trade-off: Increasing spike forgiveness in quota enforcer reduces sensitivity to real sustained overuse; mitigation is to add longer-term anomaly detection to catch malicious or sustained misuse
Follow-up: Schedule a cross-team working session (SRE, Gateway, Quota-Enforcer, Product) to finalize policy changes and test plans (target week 2025-02-24)
Retro action: Add a 'token-headroom' SLA metric per region that feeds into PagerDuty thresholds to reduce surprise 429 storms
signoffs: Diane Rosario - SRE - accepted mitigation plan 2025-02-20
